_comment: Guided tour for burst selection. The action bar is icon-only (shared action_button vocabulary), so the steps target it by objectName suffix -- {'name': 'add'} finds toolaction_add. Read by chisurf.gui.widgets.tools.guided_tour.

steps.title: The step everything else inherits
steps.text:
This window decides what a burst is. BVA, 2CDE, MLE, H2MM and every FRET histogram downstream are one row per burst found here — change a setting on this page and every later number changes with it.

Seven steps.

steps.title: The raw files
steps.text: Add TTTR files or a folder of them. They are read once here; nothing downstream re-opens them.

await.hint: Press the add button to choose files or a folder.

steps.title: The definition nothing downstream re-checks
steps.text:
The detector setup says which physical channel is donor, which is acceptor, and which excitation period each belongs to.

Get it backwards and you still get a complete, plausible analysis — with E reflected about ½ — and no fit statistic anywhere reports it. Set it against the hardware, once, and confirm it on a sample whose answer you already know.

steps.title: How the search actually works
steps.text:
A window of m consecutive photons slides along the stream; the instantaneous rate is m divided by the time they span. A burst opens where that rate rises a factor F above the local background — typically F ≈ 6, m ≈ 10 — and closes when it falls back.

Local is the whole point: laser power and buffer drift over a long acquisition, and a fixed rate threshold quietly changes what it selects as they do.

steps.title: The mistake worth naming
steps.text:
Do not put the size cut inside the search. Search permissively and apply the minimum-photon cut afterwards, on the background-corrected size.

A size cut applied during the search interacts with the threshold and biases which molecules you ever see. It removes dim ones preferentially — and dim usually correlates with exactly the thing you are trying to measure.

steps.title: Run it
steps.text: The search runs over every file, and the diagnostic tabs fill in.

steps.title: Read the diagnostics in this order
steps.text:
dT — inter-photon times. Background is a broad exponential; bursts are the short-time excess. No clear excess means there is nothing to find, and no threshold will conjure it.
Burst length — should fall smoothly. A spike at the minimum means your cut is doing the selecting.
MCS — the intensity over time: photobleaching, a drifting focus, an aggregate crossing.

Then the real test: change the threshold by a factor of two and run again. A real population survives it. The ? button has the rest.
